decision.explanation: The claim posits that the EZH2 Y646F variant is a predictive marker for resistance to Tazemetostat in B-cell lymphoma. The available evidence (pmid-25493630) demonstrates that Tazemetostat (EPZ-6438) achieves tumor growth inhibition and shows synergy with CHOP in EZH2 Y646F mutant xenografts (WSU-DLCL2). This evidence indicates efficacy, not resistance. There is no data in the provided corpus regarding resistance mechanisms, lack of efficacy, or clinical resistance outcomes for this specific variant. Therefore, the evidence is insufficient to support the claim of resistance.

citations.quote: We report here that combining EPZ-6438 with CHOP in preclinical cell culture and mouse models results in dramatic synergy for cell killing in EZH2 mutant germinal center NHL cells . . . In WSU-DLCL2 xenograft bearing mice, tumor growth inhibition (TGI) was achieved at all EPZ-6438 doses and schedules employed, and was better than CHOP alon . . . EPZ-6438/CHOP combinations show enhanced anti-tumor activity compared to single agents in several EZH2 mutant
